topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, core themes, and primary learning outcomes for cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of genetic regulation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the benign-to-malignant spectrum
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the defining features of benign and malignant tumors, focusing on local tissue invasion, metastatic dissemination, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and clinical exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of tumor-induced morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the local, anatomical, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor frequency in human populations and compare cancer occurrence across diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale, histological detection methods, and diagnostic limitations of population screening for various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing logistical instructions for upcoming practicals.
